sources.title: Redacted Direct Testimony of Kyra Coyle on Behalf of Stadion LLC, Utah PSC Docket 24-035-04
sources.notes: Sworn utility-rate testimony filed for Stadion, a Meta subsidiary and Rocky Mountain Power special-contract customer. Printed page 6 reports more than $1.5 billion invested in Utah and more than 300 operations jobs; the public copy redacts facility load and does not disclose payroll, annual capital spending, electricity use, or customer payments.

sources.title: Meta Eagle Mountain Data Center factsheet
sources.notes: Current two-page factsheet retrieved September 6, 2026. It reports more than $5.2 million in direct Utah County funding, 280-plus grants and sponsorships, and 1,719 MW across thirteen Utah clean-energy projects. It supersedes a cached 2025 edition that reported $4.1 million and 210-plus grants, but it gives no edition date, project operating dates, recipient-level reconciliation, facility load, or water-meter quantity.

sources.title: Intent to Approve DAQE-IN159410007-22, Stadion Eagle Mountain Data Center
sources.notes: The permit record identifies Stadion at 1499 North Pony Express Parkway, five existing EAG buildings, 29 existing diesel emergency generators, and a proposal for fourteen additional generators serving two UCO buildings. It is an intent-to-approve document rather than evidence that the proposed generators were finally authorized or commissioned; potential emissions and maximum testing hours are not actual use.

sources.title: Datacenter water now re-used for Wride park grass
sources.notes: City account of the Meta cooling-water reuse project begun in 2020. The City says it was responsible for necessary filtration and booster-station infrastructure and that the investments totaled around $5 million; the article does not separate Meta, city, utility, or other funding shares or recurring costs.

sources.title: Eagle Mountain City Water Conservation and Management Plan
sources.notes: The adopted plan reports that the first reuse line and booster station were operating for the 2024 irrigation season and displaced 77,715,648 gallons of potable irrigation water. That avoided municipal withdrawal is not Meta facility consumption, a water right, a utility payment, or an annual project operating-cost measure.

sources.title: Utah County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report 2023
sources.notes: The statistical section's principal-property-taxpayer table is sourced to the Utah County Treasurer and reports values in thousands. Stadion LLC is ranked fifth for 2023 at $305.404 million, or 0.35 percent of total county taxable assessed value; the table is not a tax bill, cash receipt, parcel roll, or campus-only valuation.

sources.title: EM Chamber opens dynamic Launch Pad incubator
sources.notes: City announcement identifies a $250,000 Meta/Facebook grant supporting the Eagle Mountain Chamber of Commerce Launch Pad. It does not give a transfer date, audited payment record, or outcomes attributable to the grant, and the amount overlaps Meta's later cumulative community total.

sources.title: Meta Platforms, Inc. 2021 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1, List of Subsidiaries
sources.notes: Meta's filed subsidiary list includes Stadion LLC. The filing establishes corporate identity but contains no Eagle Mountain asset, employment, supplier, utility, tax, or project-cost breakdown.

sources.title: Eagle Mountain Redevelopment Agency interlocal-agreement meeting materials
sources.notes: Agreement bundle describes contingent tax-increment participation percentages, phase durations, and real-property reimbursement caps for the original Stadion project area. The terms are ceilings and formulas, not proof of annual taxes diverted, payments received by Stadion, public-service expenditures, or net fiscal benefit.

sources.title: Master Infrastructure Agreement between Eagle Mountain City and Stadion LLC
sources.notes: Agreement governs off-site roads, review and inspection staffing, and later infrastructure orders. It says Stadion constructs approved infrastructure or reimburses City costs, but the reviewed public agreement gives no completed Stadion payment ledger, supplier invoice, locally retained share, or complete city cost series.

sources.title: Eagle Mountain City Fiscal Year 2024 Budget
sources.notes: Page 15 says Facebook had invested more than $100 million in infrastructure under the 2018 agreement, including a substation bringing 1,000 MW of regional delivery capacity. The statement does not provide an asset schedule, payment recipient, completion dates, public/private ownership, or allocation between the campus and regional growth, so it is not normalized separately from the broader campus-investment total.

sources.title: Rocky Mountain Power adds three new solar facilities in Utah for Facebook
sources.notes: Utility release describes three 235 MW Utah projects under Schedule 34 and 694 MW of signed in-state solar supporting Facebook's regional data centers. It does not identify Eagle Mountain meter load, annual generation delivered, project exclusivity, customer cost, or the operating status of every later Meta-supported project.

sources.title: Our approach to water restoration
sources.notes: Meta's portfolio table associates the Eagle Mountain data center with 415.8 million gallons per year of Provo River flow-restoration benefit and 467.4 million gallons per year at Hobble Creek. These are modeled or contracted watershed benefits rather than facility water consumption, withdrawals, wastewater volume, water rights, or verified net basin impact.

sources.title: AGC of Utah Contractors Look Forward to More Growth in 2019
sources.notes: Construction trade coverage identifies Minneapolis-based Mortenson as builder and Forterra Structural Precast's Utah offices as supplying insulated precast panels. It reports no contract values, invoice amounts, worker residence, payroll, or Utah County share and therefore cannot support a supplier-spending observation.

sources.title: Facebook fires up first data center operations in Utah as massive construction project continues
sources.notes: Contemporaneous local reporting corroborates first-phase operation and continued multi-building construction. Its 1.5-million-square-foot completion figure conflicts with Meta's contemporaneous nearly 2.4-million-square-foot campus statement, so neither secondary figure is used to allocate the selected IM3 footprint.

project_updates.title: Identity and facility boundary audit — one IM3 footprint inside a larger Stadion campus
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: SEC Exhibits 21 for 2021-2025, Utah PSC dockets 20-035-04 and 24-035-04, Utah DEQ source N159410007, Meta's Eagle Mountain pages, IM3 building inventory, Utah County land records, and Eagle Mountain city records for 2018-2026. Queries used Meta, Facebook, Stadion LLC, Eagle Mountain Data Center, EAG1-EAG7, UCO, 1499 North Pony Express Parkway, 1275 North Community Circle, and the original parcel numbers 59:057:0003/0004. Stadion is a Meta subsidiary and the operator record resolves to the campus, but no public crosswalk maps IM3 building 01024051963 to an EAG identifier; all campus values remain unallocated. No public-record requests were made.
project_updates.project_description: Meta’s Eagle Mountain Data Center is a multi-building campus at 1499 North Pony Express Parkway in Eagle Mountain, Utah County, operated through Meta subsidiary Stadion LLC. The selected inventory target is one 344,790-square-foot IM3 building footprint within that campus; public records do not map the footprint to Meta’s EAG building identifiers, so campus-wide values remain unallocated. The campus broke ground in 2018 and began serving traffic in July 2021, while later expansion areas are kept outside this project unless a source explicitly establishes continuity.

project_updates.title: Operator and regulatory disclosures — later actual anchors replace two opening forecasts
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta opening releases, current and cached factsheets, Meta annual sustainability materials, SEC 10-Ks and subsidiary exhibits, and Utah PSC Stadion testimony and exhibits from 2020-2026. Queries used Eagle Mountain investment, capex, operations jobs, employee, FTE, payroll, wage, revenue, expense, special contract, reserved capacity, demand and load. The 2024 sworn filing supports cumulative investment above $1.5 billion and more than 300 operations jobs, while the 2021 more-than-$1-billion and more-than-200-job values remain correctly labeled source forecasts. No annual capex, depreciation, campus revenue, operating expense, filled direct FTE, payroll, wage or building allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Construction and permit audit — equipment counts retained without converting permits to spend
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Utah DAQ permits N159410005, N159410007 and the 2026 N159410011 status entry; Eagle Mountain building and planning portals; Utah public-meeting packets; Meta construction releases; ENR coverage; and address/building-ID searches from 2018-2026. The December 2022 record lists 29 existing generators and fourteen proposed units for two buildings, preserved with separate bases. Meta's 2021 opening release reports a 1,250-worker historical peak while a later factsheet says 1,200; the baseline 1,250 observation is retained and the conflict documented rather than averaged. No permit valuation, contract total, completion invoice, worker hours, residence, payroll, or building-specific construction expenditure was found.

project_updates.title: Supplier audit — firms are identifiable but local spending is not
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: ENR/AGC coverage, Mortenson project and safety coverage, city permit and infrastructure materials, Meta partner pages, procurement/vendor searches, and named-company searches for 2018-2026. ENR identifies Mortenson as builder and Forterra Structural Precast's Utah offices as an insulated-panel supplier; the infrastructure agreement also mentions Psomas review and inspection staffing. No source reports contract values, invoices, supplier payments, Utah County establishment addresses, worker residence, procurement totals, or a locally retained purchasing share. The supplier channel therefore remains missing rather than being inferred from firm names.

project_updates.title: Electric utility audit — supporting capacity is not facility consumption
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Rocky Mountain Power Schedule 34 releases and Utah tariffs; PSC dockets 20-035-04, 24-035-04 and large-load line-extension materials; Meta renewable-energy reports and factsheets; EIA facility and utility datasets; and searches for Stadion meter, kWh, MWh, MW, peak demand, bill and rate from 2018-2026. The current operator factsheet describes thirteen Utah projects adding 1,719 MW, retained only as an unallocated source projection. The PSC filing confirms special-contract service but redacts facility load. No actual campus kWh, billed demand, annual electricity payment, PUE, renewable generation delivered, or selected-building meter was public.

project_updates.title: Water and wastewater audit — reuse benefit is measurable, campus withdrawal is not
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Eagle Mountain's 2018 Stadion water/sewer agreement index, 2022 infrastructure agreement, 2024 reuse article and conservation plan, Meta 2023-2024 water-benefit reports, Utah Division of Water Rights listings and mail logs, and Division of Water Quality materials. Queries covered Stadion, Facebook, Meta, 1499 Pony Express, cooling water, wastewater, reuse, withdrawal, consumption, acre-feet, gallons and water rights from 2018-2026. The city reports 77,715,648 gallons of potable irrigation displacement in 2024 and Meta reports watershed-restoration benefits, but neither is facility use. Water-right records 54-459/54-1470 name Eagle Mountain Data Center Campus LLC, not Stadion/Meta, and were excluded as a separate developer. No Meta meter, annual withdrawal, consumptive use, sewer volume, rate or payment was found.

project_updates.title: Fiscal and assessor audit — taxpayer value is observed, tax cash flows are not
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Utah County 2023 ACFR and 2025 budget statistical tables, county land-record abstracts and property-search entry points, Alpine School District budgets, original and current parcel searches, and owner-name searches for Stadion LLC and Meta from 2018-2026. Utah County reports $305.404 million of 2023 taxable assessed value for Stadion. An Alpine School District table reports $358.043091 million under its own principal-taxpayer presentation; the two bases cannot be reconciled from the public tables, so only the county-wide value is normalized. No parcel/account roll tying the full value to the campus, property-tax bill, payment, distribution, exemption amount, personal-property split, or annual series was found.

project_updates.title: Incentive and public-cost audit — contingent terms do not establish realized subsidy
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Sweetwater Industrial Park CRA #1 plan, budget, participation agreement, and interlocal amendments; 2018 approved minutes; city budgets for FY2019-FY2024; county and school materials; and searches for Stadion reimbursement, tax increment, PILOT, grant, incentive, disbursement and service cost through 2026. Agreements specify participation percentages, 20-year phase periods, a 40-year outside limit, and entity-specific real-property caps while personal-property reimbursement remains formula-driven. No realized annual tax increment, Stadion reimbursement ledger, service-cost series, grant disbursement, or same-scope fiscal net was found. The roughly $5 million city-built reuse project is a bounded gross project cost with unresolved funding, not the complete public cost of the campus.

project_updates.title: Land, infrastructure, bond and court audit — obligations found, cash evidence absent
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: original county parcels 59:057:0003/0004 and subdivision abstracts, 2018 development and water/sewer agreement indexes, the 2022 Master Infrastructure Agreement and orders, Eagle Mountain budgets and capital materials, Utah Treasurer/Finance Commission bond materials, Utah court/public-index searches, SEC filings, and exact Stadion/entity/address searches for 2018-2026. The agreement allocates construction or reimbursement duties for off-site infrastructure but contains no completed payment schedule; a $1.8 million Pony Express resurfacing item is expressly associated with Google reimbursement and was excluded. No project bond, mortgage amount, litigation recovery, mechanics-lien total, deed consideration, completed public advance, or Stadion reimbursement amount was found.

project_updates.title: Expansion audit — later phases are not silently folded into the selected project
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: city and Utah public-notice records for Sweetwater CRA areas #1-#4, Stadion South Expansion, 2025 development agreements, 2026 notices, parcel-owner tables, DEQ N159410011, and contemporary operator/trade reporting. The original operating campus, later UCO buildings, the southern expansion and other Eagle Mountain data-center projects occupy distinct records and sometimes distinct parcels. New QTS, Google, Tract, Williams and Sweetwater #2/#4 values were excluded unless a source explicitly tied them to the original Meta operating campus. The project account therefore does not treat all Stadion-owned land or every later agreement as one realized facility.

project_updates.title: Community audit — cumulative and named-recipient amounts are kept overlap-aware
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta factsheets and opening release, Community Action Grant recipient pages for 2019-2026, Eagle Mountain city announcements, Alpine School District and Utah nonprofit pages, and searches for grant, donation, sponsorship, school, nonprofit, volunteer and recipient amounts. The current factsheet reports more than $5.2 million to Utah County schools and nonprofits and 280-plus grants/sponsorships; the city independently reports a $250,000 Launch Pad grant. Because Launch Pad is part of the cumulative program, the observations are retained but flagged against summation. No full annual ledger, in-kind valuation, recipient reconciliation, volunteer-hour value, or causal community outcome was found.

project_updates.title: Journalism and trade-press audit — corroboration retained as search evidence, not preferred measurements
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: KSL/Deseret News, FOX13, Engineering News-Record, Data Center Dynamics/indexed trade coverage, contractor pages and local reporting from announcement through September 2026. Queries combined Meta/Facebook/Stadion with Eagle Mountain, construction, opening, expansion, contractor, supplier, jobs, tax, power and water. Reporting corroborates the July 2021 opening and identifies contractors, but repeats operator estimates or conflicts on campus floor area (about 1.5 million versus Meta's nearly 2.4 million square feet). No unique, better-supported payment, employment, payroll, utility-use, tax, supplier-spend or public-cost observation survived preference for primary records.

project_updates.title: Government-statistics and county-outcome audit — no defensible comparison model retained
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: the governed 2001-2024 county economic panel, BEA CAEMP25N/CAINC/real-GDP regional files, BLS QCEW county employment and wage files, Census County Business Patterns, and Utah economic-development context. Utah County has rapid population growth, semiconductor and technology investment, multiple data-center projects, and no source-registered untreated comparison group or clean campus-only treatment date; the July 2021 opening also overlaps continuing construction and later phases. A before/after change or ad hoc county match would be descriptive but materially confounded, so GDP, employment and wage comparison-gap modules remain absent rather than being presented as Meta effects.

project_updates.title: Contribution-account disposition — direct anchors improved, unsupported channels remain open
project_updates.notes: After deduplication, direct observations cover construction, investment, operations, fiscal, resources and community. Supplier spending remains unobserved; public-cost evidence is limited to a roughly $5 million city-built reuse project whose funding shares and recurring costs are undisclosed, so it does not satisfy the full public-cost category or permit net-fiscal synthesis. Facility electricity and water use, direct FTE/payroll, annual capex, tax payments, realized incentive reimbursements and all three county comparison modules remain unresolved. No construction multiplier, arbitrary local share, operating multiplier, property-tax estimate, utility-use estimate, fiscal net, or causal county effect was created.
